title: Hwang–Jang–Oh web-permutation enumeration conjecture
statement:
A **web permutation** is a permutation characterized by the property that each of its cycles is an André cycle. Let $\mathrm{Web}_n$ be the set of web permutations in $\mathfrak{S}_n$, let $M(\sigma)$ be the matching associated with $\sigma$, and define

$$
M_0^{(n)}:=\{\{0,1\},\{2,3\},\ldots,\{2n-2,2n-1\}\}.
$$

Set $\widetilde{\mathrm{Web}}_n:=\{\sigma\in\mathrm{Web}_n:M(\sigma)=M_0^{(n)}\}$, and let $f(n,k)$ be the number of $\sigma\in\widetilde{\mathrm{Web}}_n$ with $\sigma_1=k$. The Seidel triangle $(s_{i,j})_{i,j\geq1}$ is defined by $s_{1,1}=s_{2,1}=1$ and

$$
s_{i,j}=0\quad\text{if }j=0\text{ or }j>\lceil i/2\rceil,
$$

$$
s_{2i+1,j}=s_{2i+1,j-1}+s_{2i,j}\quad\text{for }j=1,2,\dots,i+1,
$$

$$
s_{2i,j}=s_{2i,j+1}+s_{2i-1,j}\quad\text{for }j=1,2,\dots,i.
$$

**Hwang–Jang–Oh's conjecture.** For $n\geq1$, the enumerative values satisfy

$$
\begin{cases} f(2n-1,2k-1)=s_{2n-2,k}, \\ f(2n,2k-1)=s_{2n-1,n-k+1}. \end{cases}
$$

The conjecture gives a Seidel-triangle interpretation of refined counts of web permutations with the distinguished matching $M_0^{(n)}$. The source paper states that it proves this enumerative conjecture, so it is solved.
source_name: Yao Dong, Zhicong Lin and Qiongqiong Pan, “Web permutations, Seidel triangle and normalized γ-coefficients”, arXiv:2502.01161 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01161

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2025). “In this work, we prove the enumerative conjecture of Hwang-Jang-Oh and answer the two open problems proposed by Xu and Zeng.”
